title: MAKING INTRODUCTIONS
conversation: At the dinner party, Lisa introduces Lori and Mike to Jane and Kyle Chen. Lori and Jane realize they’ve met previously through work. Lisa: Let me make some introductions. Lori and Mike Garcia, this is Jane and Kyle Chen. Lori: Nice to meet you. Kyle: I’m sorry, I didn’t catch your names. Lori: I’m Lori and this is my husband Mike. Lisa: You guys have a lot in common, so I’m sure you’ll hit it off. Jane: Lori, you look familiar, but I can’t quite place you. Lori: Your name rings a bell. Do you work at Harco Insurance? Jane: I used to be in sales there. I left about a year ago. Lori: I used to work at Comtek International. You sold us our insurance plan. Jane: Yes, that’s right! It’s a small world! Lori: It sure is. I’m glad we’ve crossed paths again. Jane: Me too. What have you been up to since you left Comtek? Lori: It’s a long story. Let’s grab some drinks and I’ll fill you in.

idioms.meaning_en: To introduce people to each other by name for the first time
idioms.meaning_vi: giới thiệu ai đó với ai đó
idioms.example: Before we start the meeting, let me make some introductions.
idioms.fill_sentence: I noticed that most of the new team members hadn't met each other yet when they arrived at the meeting. I decided to step in and make some introductions so that everyone felt comfortable working together. Once everyone knew each other's names, the project discussion became much more productive.

idioms.meaning_en: I didn't hear your name when you were introduced
idioms.meaning_vi: tôi đã không nghe rõ tên bạn
idioms.example: I'm sorry, the room was so loud that I didn't catch your names.
idioms.context: I’m sorry, I didn’t catch your names.
idioms.fill_sentence: I am so sorry, but I didn’t catch your names when you were introduced earlier at the meeting. Could you please introduce yourselves again so I can make sure I have the correct spelling for my notes?

idioms.meaning_en: - to share similar interests or have similar backgrounds
idioms.example: My best friend and I have a lot in common, especially our love for music.
idioms.context: You guys have a lot in common, so I’m sure you’ll hit it off.
idioms.fill_sentence: When Mai and Lan first met at the university club, they discovered they both loved classical music and grew up in the same small town. Because they share so many similar hobbies and life experiences, it is clear that they have a lot in common. They decided to become roommates shortly after.

idioms.meaning_en: To get along very well with someone from the first time you meet them
idioms.meaning_vi: tâm đầu ý hợp / nhanh chóng trở nên thân thiết
idioms.example: I introduced my two cousins, and they really hit it off.
idioms.context: You guys have a lot in common, so I’m sure you’ll hit it off.
idioms.fill_sentence: I was nervous about meeting my new roommate today, but we started talking about our shared love for jazz music immediately. We really hit it off within the first ten minutes and decided to go get dinner together. It feels like we have been friends for years already.

idioms.meaning_en: To seem like someone or something you have seen or known before
idioms.example: You look familiar; did we go to the same high school?
idioms.context: Lori, you look familiar, but I can’t quite place you.
idioms.fill_sentence: I was walking through the crowded airport when I spotted a man waving at me. His face seemed to look familiar, but I could not recall his name until I remembered he was my old roommate from college.

idioms.meaning_en: I've seen (or met) you before, but I can't remember where or when
idioms.meaning_vi: Tôi đã gặp bạn ở đâu đó, nhưng tôi không thể nhớ chính xác là ở đâu hoặc khi nào
idioms.example: I recognize your voice, but I can't quite place you.
idioms.context: Lori, you look familiar, but I can’t quite place you.
idioms.fill_sentence: I was walking through the supermarket yesterday when a friendly man approached me and started a casual conversation. I recognized his face from somewhere, but despite staring at him for a moment, I had to admit, "I can’t quite place you." Could you remind me where we have met before?

idioms.meaning_en: To sound familiar, or remind you of something you've heard before
idioms.meaning_vi: nghe quen quen / gợi nhớ đến điều gì
idioms.example: The name of that restaurant rings a bell, but I don't think I've eaten there.
idioms.fill_sentence: I looked at the stranger's face for a long time, trying to remember where we had met before. Although I could not recall his name, his smile seemed to ring a bell. I felt certain that we had been classmates in primary school many years ago.

idioms.meaning_en: to work in a sales position
idioms.meaning_vi: làm trong bộ phận bán hàng/kinh doanh
idioms.example: She has been in sales for over ten years.
idioms.context: I used to be in sales there.
idioms.fill_sentence: My brother just landed a new position at a large tech company. He spends his entire day calling potential clients to convince them to buy the software. He is really enjoying his new job in sales.

idioms.meaning_en: This expression is used when people are surprised to find out they know each other from some past experience
idioms.meaning_vi: Thế giới quả thật nhỏ bé! (Tình cờ gặp lại nhau)
idioms.example: I saw my old neighbor in Paris; it's a small world!
idioms.context: Yes, that’s right! It’s a small world!
idioms.fill_sentence: I was attending a business conference in Tokyo when I suddenly bumped into my former high school teacher from Hanoi. I had no idea he was even in Japan, let alone at the same event. I told him, "It’s a small world," as we both laughed at the incredible coincidence.

idioms.meaning_en: To meet someone, usually by chance or accident
idioms.example: We first crossed paths at a technology conference last year.
idioms.context: I’m glad we’ve crossed paths again.
idioms.fill_sentence: I have lived in this busy city for five years and never expected to see my childhood friend again. It was purely a coincidence that we managed to cross paths at the local grocery store yesterday. We were both shocked to bump into each other in the produce aisle after all this time.

idioms.idiom: What have you been up to
idioms.meaning_en: A common way to ask what someone has been doing lately
idioms.meaning_vi: Dạo này bạn làm gì rồi?
idioms.example: It's been a long time! What have you been up to?
idioms.context: What have you been up to since you left Comtek?
idioms.fill_sentence: I haven't seen you at the library since the semester started last month. It has been such a long time, so tell me, what have you been up to lately? I really want to hear all about what you have been doing with your free time.

idioms.meaning_en: Used to indicate that something is complicated and would take a long time to explain fully
idioms.meaning_vi: đó là một câu chuyện dài (khó giải thích nhanh)
idioms.example: Why did I quit my job? It's a long story.
idioms.fill_sentence: My friend asked me why I ended up missing the final exam and having to walk home in the rain. I sighed because there were too many complex details to cover about the bus breakdown and my lost bag. I told him, "It’s a long story," and suggested we talk about it later over coffee.

idioms.meaning_en: To get something to drink; to go out for a drink
idioms.meaning_vi: đi mua đồ uống / đi uống nước
idioms.example: Let's grab some drinks after work on Friday.
idioms.context: Let’s grab some drinks and I’ll fill you in.
idioms.fill_sentence: We finally finished that exhausting project after working late hours at the office. Everyone is tired and wants to unwind, so we decided to head to the bar nearby to grab some drinks together. It will be nice to relax and chat before we head home for the night.

idioms.meaning_en: To update someone; to tell somebody what's been going on
idioms.meaning_vi: cập nhật cho ai đó; kể cho ai đó nghe chuyện đã xảy ra
idioms.example: I missed the meeting, so could you fill me in on what happened?
idioms.context: Let’s grab some drinks and I’ll fill you in.
idioms.fill_sentence: I missed the entire team meeting this morning because I was stuck in a dentist appointment. Could you please fill me in on what was discussed during the project briefing?
